title: Quasi-coherent algebra descent along a general smooth scheme atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Let $p:U\to\mathcal X$ be a smooth surjective scheme atlas and put $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$, with projections $p_1,p_2:R\to U$ and diagonal $e:U\to R$. These are $2$-fibre products [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; $R$ and the triple relation space are algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], not required to be schemes. Restriction gives an equivalence between quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebras [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] and pairs $(C,\delta)$ consisting of a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_U$-algebra $C$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and an algebra isomorphism $\delta:p_1^*C\simeq p_2^*C$ satisfying $e^*\delta=1$ and $p_{23}^*\delta\circ p_{12}^*\delta=p_{13}^*\delta$ on $U\times_{\mathcal X}U\times_{\mathcal X}U$. Pullbacks are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. Morphisms on the right are all algebra maps commuting with $\delta$; thus objects and maps descend uniquely up to the compatible isomorphism. This equivalence is compatible with restriction along smooth scheme tests and with tensor products, the unit algebra and their structural maps. A descended map is injective on the smooth-etale site if its map on $U$ is injective as a map of quasi-coherent sheaves; conversely injection on that site implies injection on $U$. This last assertion makes no claim of injectivity after nonflat big-site pullback. No quasi-compactness, finite presentation, affine-relation, or Deligne--Mumford hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06WV (lemma-quasi-coherent-algebraic-stack), parts (1) and (5), and Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent). Algebra objects follow by the tensor-compatible equivalence; injection on smooth tests uses flatness of smooth pullback, as in stacks-cohomology.tex Tag 0GQF (lemma-quasi-coherent-check-exact).

proof.text: Put $s=p_1,t=p_2$. Smoothness implies flatness and local finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Thus [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations](2) applies to the given smooth surjective scheme atlas: its self-relation is an algebraic space, with groupoid operations given by composition of the specified isomorphisms, and $[U/R]\simeq\mathcal X$ compatibly with $U$. Let $\mathcal P$ be the groupoid prestack with objects $u:T\to U$ and arrows $(f,r):(T,u)\to(T',u')$, where $f:T\to T'$, $r:T\to R$, $sr=u$ and $tr=u'f$. Its stackification is $[U/R]$. For an algebra on $\mathcal X$, [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] gives the quasi-coherent algebra on each scheme test; the arrow $(u,v,\alpha)$ in the self-relation induces its pullback isomorphism. Identity and composition of these arrows give exactly the displayed unit and triple-cocycle equations. This constructs restriction, including its action on all algebra maps.

source.place: Tags 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), first construction, and 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent); algebraic.tex Tags 04T5 and 04WY.

proof.text: Conversely, fix $(C,\delta)$ on $U$. On $\mathcal P$ set $H(T,u)=\Gamma(T,u^*C)$, with its usual algebra structure. For $(f,r)$ define restriction as section pullback along $f$ followed by $r^*\delta^{-1}:(u'f)^*C\to u^*C$. The scheme section pullbacks and their composition comparisons are those of [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence]. Two successive arrows have transition $r_1^*\delta^{-1}\circ r_2^*\delta^{-1}=(\delta_{r_2}\circ\delta_{r_1})^{-1}=\delta_{r_2r_1}^{-1}$ under these comparisons. This is the single restriction for their composite, by the given cocycle; the identity restriction is the identity by $e^*\delta=1$. All restrictions are ring maps over pullback of functions, since $\delta$ is an algebra isomorphism. These formulas therefore define a presheaf of commutative algebras, not just its values on objects.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), reverse construction, restriction formula and omitted presheaf check.

proof.text: For $x=(T,u)$, its slice in $\mathcal P$ is equivalent to schemes over $T$: an arrow to $x$ is uniquely isomorphic over $x$ to the chosen cartesian arrow over its base map, because all vertical arrows are invertible. Under this equivalence the restriction of $H$ is $A_T(u^*C)$, using the transition isomorphism in step 2. By [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence] this is an fppf sheaf with local free presentations. Hence $H$ is a sheaf: every covering and its matching sections lie in such a slice. It is quasi-coherent as defined in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]: the local free presentations on each slice give precisely a covering and presentation locally at every object of $\mathcal P$. No descent theorem on a nonexistent scheme representing $R$ is used here; a map $T\to R$ suffices for the restriction formula.

source.place: Tags 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), reverse construction, and 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent), proof by the local-presentation definition.

proof.text: Let $q:\mathcal P\to[U/R]\simeq\mathcal X$. By [lem-sfb-stackification-module-equivalence], precomposition gives an equivalence on all module sheaves, restricting to quasi-coherent ones. It therefore descends the underlying module of $H$ to a quasi-coherent module $F$, with $q^*F\simeq H$. We also need its actual tensor comparison. For quasi-coherent $F,G$ on $\mathcal X$, [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness] ensures that $F\otimes G$ and the unit are quasi-coherent. On the slice of $x\in\mathcal P(T)$, [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] identifies the restrictions with $A_T(F_{qx})$ and $A_T(G_{qx})$. Apply [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] on both sites and the tensor comparison of [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence]. Both $q^*(F\otimes G)$ and $q^*F\otimes q^*G$ then identify with $A_T(F_{qx}\otimes G_{qx})$. The canonical comparison sends each local pure tensor to that same tensor, so it is this isomorphism on every slice, hence globally. The unit comparison is the identity on $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Associativity, symmetry and unit compatibility follow on local pure tensors: either composite sends $(a\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $a\otimes(b\otimes c)$, or exchanges the same factors, or multiplies the same scalar. Such sections locally generate the sheaf tensor.

source.place: Tags 06WQ (lemma-stackification), 06WR (lemma-stackification-quasi-coherent), 06WV(5), 06WK; tensor comparisons on the localized scheme sites.

proof.text: The multiplication of $H$ is bilinear and thus a module map $H\otimes H\to H$ by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. Using step 4's tensor and unit comparisons, full faithfulness of [lem-sfb-stackification-module-equivalence] gives unique maps $\mu:F\otimes F\to F$ and $\eta:\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to F$ restricting to multiplication and unit of $H$. The two associativity maps from $F^{\otimes3}$, the two unit diagrams and the commutativity diagram become the corresponding equalities for $H$ after $q^*$. Faithfulness makes these equalities hold on $\mathcal X$. The same bilinear universal property interprets $\mu$ as a sheaf multiplication; with $\eta$ it makes $F$ a commutative algebra in exactly the sense of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Thus the construction descends its algebra operations as well as its module.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent) applied to multiplication and unit, with Tag 06WR; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK, tensor universal property.

proof.text: A compatible map $h:C\to D$ gives $H_C(T,u)\to H_D(T,u)$ by $\Gamma(T,u^*h)$; compatibility with $\delta$ is precisely commutation with the restriction along every $(f,r)$. Conversely a module map $H_C\to H_D$ restricts on the slice of $(U,1)$, identified with $(\mathit{Sch}/U)_{fppf}$, to a unique module map $h:C\to D$ by [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence]. Naturality along $(f,e)$ forces its components to be $\Gamma(T,u^*h)$; naturality along $(1,r)$ forces the descent equation. This tests the equation on all scheme maps to $R$, in particular on its etale scheme charts, so it is an equation on $R$. The map is an algebra map exactly when it preserves multiplication and unit on every slice, equivalently when $h$ does, by the tensor comparison and faithfulness of that scheme equivalence. Finally [lem-sfb-stackification-module-equivalence] descends these module maps uniquely; faithfulness and step 4 show that the descended maps preserve the operations of step 5. This proves full faithfulness on all algebra maps, not only isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), both functors, with the omitted morphism and quasi-inverse checks written explicitly.

proof.text: Restriction of the constructed algebra to $U$ is $C$: on the slice $(U,1)$ the sheaf is $A_U(C)$, whose inverse comparison is the identity on Zariski opens by [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence]; the arrows $r$ recover $\delta$ by the formula in step 2. Starting instead with an algebra $B$ on $\mathcal X$, [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] identifies its value at every $(T,u)$ with $\Gamma(T,u^*B_U)$, and its restrictions with the same $r^*\delta^{-1}$ formula. Thus the presheaf constructed from its datum is canonically $q^*B$, on maps and operations. Full faithfulness of [lem-sfb-stackification-module-equivalence] descends this identification to the unique compatible algebra isomorphism with $B$. These identifications are natural by their section formulas, so the two constructions are quasi-inverse.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), final omitted quasi-inverse verification; Tags 06WK and 06WR.

proof.text: For a scheme test $a:T\to\mathcal X$, [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] identifies restriction with tensor pullback and gives its natural identity and composition comparisons, preserving the structure module and tensors. Thus the restriction functor of step 1 carries an algebra tensor product to the tensor product of its two restrictions, with transition $\delta_C\otimes\delta_D$, and carries the unit to the canonical unit datum. Multiplication on $C\otimes D$ sends $(c\otimes d)(c'\otimes d')$ to $cc'\otimes dd'$, and its unit is $1\otimes1$; these are exactly the restrictions of the same structural maps on the descended algebras. The comparisons in step 4 respect these formulas. The composition comparisons for test pullback therefore show compatibility after every further smooth test and for every algebra map. No arbitrary ring of global sections is being asserted to commute with tensor: all these comparisons are sheaf tensors on the test sites.

source.place: Tags 06WV(5) and 06WK; the pullback-compatible scheme comparison underlying Tag 06WT.

proof.text: Let $b:B\to D$ be the descended map, and suppose $b_U$ is injective. Fix a smooth scheme test $a:T\to\mathcal X$. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $W\to Z=U\times_{\mathcal X}T$, possible by the atlas condition of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack] and [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The projections $W\to T$ and $W\to U$ are smooth, and the former is surjective, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]; for $W\to U$ use the smoothness of $a$. In particular both scheme maps are flat. By [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] the two pullbacks of $b_T$ and $b_U$ to $W$ coincide. Exact flat pullback from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective] makes this map injective. Put $K=\ker b_T$, a quasi-coherent Zariski module by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Exactness gives $K|_W=0$. Apply [lem-sc-flat-cover-module-isomorphism-reflection] to $0\to K$ and the flat surjective scheme cover $W\to T$: it is an isomorphism after pullback, hence before pullback. Therefore $K=0$ and $b_T$ is injective. This uses the reflection lemma only for isomorphisms, its stated conclusion.

source.place: stacks-cohomology.tex Tag 0GQF (lemma-quasi-coherent-check-exact), proof with etale scheme charts of the relation spaces.

proof.text: The smooth-etale site here has objects smooth scheme maps $T\to\mathcal X$ and coverings etale covering families over each such object. By [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] its values are the sections of the quasi-coherent scheme modules $B_T,D_T$. Step 9 makes every section map on every smooth test injective; hence the restricted sheaf map is injective. Conversely, injectivity on this site gives injectivity on every open subscheme of $U$, since these remain smooth tests; therefore $b_U$ is injective. Equivalently one can use [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] to express the test injections on the small etale site. In step 9 both projections were flat because both $U$ and $T$ were smooth over $\mathcal X$; no assertion about an arbitrary nonflat big-site test follows, or is needed.

source.place: stacks-cohomology.tex Tag 0GQF, with the smooth-test rather than big-site interpretation; stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WV(3).
